   - Contract & invoice summarization (longer context, multi-page docs)
   - Knowledge retrieval / RAG with document-level context (mixed)

2) Needs we called out:
   - Which flows require long context (32k / 128k) vs the typical 8k model?
   - Approximate monthly token volumes (prompts vs completions). If you don't have exact numbers, ballpark ranges are OK.
   - Target cost target (e.g., target $/1M tokens or an example monthly budget).

To make our pricing concrete, could you share (ideally in a quick CSV): monthly active users, avg prompts per MAU, avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, and % of traffic that will need each context length (8k/32k/128k)? An example row we use: MAU, prompts_per_user, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_completion_tokens, pct_32k, pct_128k.

As next steps we'll run a few unit-economics scenarios (hosted vs reserved capacity) and return:
  - $/1M-token pricing bands by model/config (baseline, quantized, dedicated)
  - Example monthly bill for the volumes you provide
  - Recommendations for which workloads to route to 8k vs 32k / 128k to balance cost and accuracy

I've attached a short pricing deck that explains our unit economics and what drives price differences between context lengths. If easier, feel free to reply with a CSV and Jordan (cc'd on next note) and I will build the calc.

Thanks  happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up next week after you share the numbers.

Hey Marissa  thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a quick estimate we pulled from our analytics team (exported yesterday). High level:

- MAU (product area): 120k monthly active users across chat and doc tools (combined).
- Average prompts per MAU: 6 per month (mostly chat triggers + some batch summarization).
- Avg tokens per prompt: ~140 tokens.
- Avg tokens per completion: ~620 tokens.
- Approx total tokens (current): ~100M prompt tokens / ~430M completion tokens per month (~530M total).
- Context-length needs:
   - Chat (65% of traffic) comfortably within 8k for now.
   - Summarization (20%) needs 32k for multi-page invoices and contracts.
   - Research / long-doc retrieval (15%) we expect some flows may need 128k for full-document context (but could be staged).

I've attached acme_usage_estimates.csv with the breakdown by product area + a sample export of doc sizes. Two asks:
1) Can you run a quick hosted pricing estimate for these volumes (assume baseline model quality comparable to the call) and show a delta if 15% of traffic moves to 128k?
2) Do you have recommended routing pattern (e.g., prioritize 32k for summarization and only send retrieval flows to 128k for >X page docs)?

Budget: our finance partner asked for a ballpark target of < $75k/month to start (pilot), but we can discuss committed pricing if the unit economics work.

Thanks  Alicia

Hi Alicia  really helpful, thanks for the CSV. Looping in Jordan (SE) and Vivek (pricing/ops) to validate assumptions and share the calc. Preliminary thoughts below — we'll produce a formal estimate by EOD Monday: 

1) Quick unit-econ assumptions (baseline for hosted, per 1M tokens):
   - Baseline 8k-optimized model: $900 per 1M tokens (prompt+completion combined)
   - 32k context model: +20% compute premium -> ~$1,080 per 1M tokens
   - 128k context model: +80% compute premium -> ~$1,620 per 1M tokens

2) Example monthly cost scenarios (using your current mix: 65% 8k, 20% 32k, 15% 128k):
   - Total tokens: 530M/month -> 530 * ($/1M blended)
   - Blended $/1M = 0.65*$900 + 0.20*$1,080 + 0.15*$1,620 = $ (calculate below)
   - Blended $/1M = $585 + $216 + $243 = $1,044 per 1M tokens
   - Monthly bill = 530 * $1,044 = ~$553,320/month (hosted)

3) Pilot-oriented options to get under the $75k/mo target:
   - Narrow scope: Run pilot on chat only (65% traffic) on 8k -> cost estimate ~ (0.65*530M = 344.5M tokens) * $900/1M = ~$310k/mo (still above $75k).
   - Further reductions: limit sample to a subset of MAUs (e.g., 10% of MAU) or reduce completion length via truncation/summarization.
   - Committed reserved pricing (Redwood Dedicated) can materially lower unit cost. For example, with a 6–12 month committed capacity we typically see 40–60% off hosted list pricing depending on commit and model selection.

4) Routing recommendations:
   - Route chat and short-response flows to 8k models.
   - Send document summarization to 32k; attempt document chunking + RAG to avoid blanket 128k where possible.
   - Reserve 128k for full-document ingestion where recall is critical (invoices spanning 100+ pages or full-contract analysis).

Jordan / Vivek can you validate the blended calc above and add a committed-capacity estimate for a pilot sized to ~10% of MAU (12k MAU) and one for full scale? I'll include both hosted and reserved numbers in the formal deck.

Next steps for Acme:
  - Alicia: confirm whether the pilot needs 128k at all, or if we should stage 32k first.
  - Acme: confirm the target pilot MAU (e.g., 10% of MAU) and target SLA (latency/uptime).
  - Redwood: we'll produce a formal hosted vs reserved estimate and schedule a follow-up call.

Thanks  Marissa
